f8e29347aa6b5554c832b1aea18ef044a05b9ca9.summary: eSentire's Threat Response Unit reports an intrusion that began with a fake snipping-tool download page and a Microsoft-signed store installer. That installer led to 'Setup Assistant', an obfuscated Electron app in the Microsoft Store, which acted as a backdoor executing C2-supplied PowerShell and JavaScript. It then deployed Vinci RAT, a PowerShell-based RAT with remote and reverse shell access, file staging, and several execution methods. Persistence used a scheduled task, and an AMSI bypass was observed. The report says Microsoft found the app did not violate its terms despite the TRU…

Their payloads are almost identical, and the report believes one affiliate uploaded samples for both in late December 2024. f8b96ffcca3cb99951989dd6fd28f71dcf942967.summary: CrowdStrike's incident-response account of the 2016 breach of the Democratic National Committee network. It says it was engaged on April 30, 2016, and identified two Russian-linked actors, COZY BEAR and FANCY BEAR, on the network. Remediation ran June 10 to 13, 2016. The report attributes the intrusion to the Russian government, citing a 2017 US assessment and a 2020 Senate report. Exfiltration is supported only by circumstantial indicators. Tools named include SeaDaddy, X-Agent and X-Tunnel.
